Hi Samir —

We had the 3:00 PM PT office hours today but it looks like the session went unattended. No problem — happy to help asynchronously or rebook a dedicated slot. I pulled together a very short checklist that will get us to a working call quickly if you want to try again: (attached as redwood_quickstart-checklist.pdf)

Quick troubleshooting checklist (2–5 minutes):
- Confirm REDWOOD_API_KEY is set in your environment (echo $REDWOOD_API_KEY).
- Ensure you’re using SDK v0.9.x or later (we include a minimal curl example below).
- If you see 401s, check that the key hasn’t been rotated in your org console and that the request header is exactly: Authorization: Bearer <KEY>.
- If you get a 422 / model error, send a short request body and I’ll check model mapping.

Minimal curl to sanity-check the network: 

curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_API_KEY" \n  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \n  https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -d '{"model":"redwood-1.0","input":"hi"}'

Proposed follow-up slots (PT):

- Fri Jun 3, 10:00 AM PT

Reply with a preferred time or, if you prefer, send the 401/trace log and we’ll triage asynchronously. If you want us to jump on the call we can escalate to an engineer — @Dev is CC’d.

Hi Samir —

Thanks for the trace — that looks like a straightforward auth mismatch. A couple of things to try (I’ll keep this short):

1) Confirm header format (literal):
   Authorization: Bearer <YOUR_KEY>
   (no extra quotes, no trailing spaces)

2) Check key scope in the console: if the key was created for a different project, it won’t be valid against the org-level endpoint. From the console you can:
   - Go to Settings → API Keys → find the key → Project scope.
   - If scoped to project X, either generate a new org token or call the project-scoped endpoint.

3) Quick diagnostic curl I recommend running locally: 

curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -d '{"model":"redwood-1.0","input":"health-check"}'

From your trace I see a 401 returned before model routing, so routing/kv is not the issue. If you want a short-lived test key we can generate one for you to rule out rotation — I can create an ephemeral key that expires in 1 hour and post it to this thread (or send via secure link). Which do you prefer?

If you’d like another synchronous slot, I’ve blocked 9:00 AM PT on Thu Jun 2 for Neha and can join. Here’s a direct booking link if you want to confirm: https://calendar.redwood.ai/neha/book?slot=20270602T09:00Z

If you prefer async, send the name of the key you used (redwood keys in the console show a short-id like key_abc123) and I’ll check its scope.

—Dev
